memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Speak to the Israelites and say to them: 'If a man or woman wants to make a special vow, a vow of dedication to the Lord as a Nazirite.'" - Num 6:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God makes room for something beautiful here: a person could choose to set themselves apart to the Lord in a special way through a Nazirite vow. What is striking is that this was voluntary. God did not command it of everyone; He simply made a way for those whose hearts longed to draw nearer to Him.

Notice too the gracious openness of it — "a man or woman." This special devotion was not reserved for priests or leaders or a particular tribe. It was open to anyone, male or female, whose heart was stirred to dedicate themselves more fully to God. In a world that often limited who could draw near, this was a gift of grace.

There is something wonderful about voluntary, wholehearted devotion. God welcomes not only the obedience He commands, but also the love that overflows and says, "Lord, I want to give You more." That kind of freely-chosen devotion delights His heart.

Under the new covenant, we are all invited into this kind of nearness. We do not take Nazirite vows, but every believer is called to offer themselves wholly to God as "a living sacrifice" (Rom 12:1). This is not forced religion; it is the glad response of a heart that loves God.

Is there a stirring in your heart to draw nearer to God, to give Him more of yourself? That desire is precious. Do not ignore it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is there a longing in your heart to draw nearer to God?
- What might wholehearted, voluntary devotion look like for you?
- How does it encourage you that this nearness is open to all?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You welcome hearts that long to draw near. Stir in me a glad, voluntary devotion, and help me to give You more of myself. Amen.
